cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a classic strip-woven kente cloth with the characteristic red, yellow, green and black geometric weft-float patterning arranged in checkerboard blocks between plain warp-striped bands, exactly matching Asante kente construction described in the metadata; the object is clearly and fully visible on a plain background.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Man's rectangular cloth (Asante kente), made up from 12 narrow strips hand-woven from rayon yarn, and then hand- sewn together selvedge to selvedge. The warp pattern is the same in all 12 strips: a base of red yarn with two wide stripes of yellow and green running through it. Both ends of the cloth have complex weft-faced matching patterns, and the warp ends have been left loose to form a fringe. Across the face of the central area of the cloth have been introduced regularly-spaced weft blocks arranged to form a chequerboard alternation with the warp pattern. The weft blocks themselves are made of yellow, black, red, and green yarn, with varied discontinuous supplementary weft patterns introduced between flanking solid blocks of colour.
